boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten named Boulder places for a no-purchase hang, using documented free admission or the City’s no-fee open-access policy.

cards.title: Browse the CU Art Museum
cards.subtitle: Visual Arts Complex, CU Boulder
cards.notes: Meet outside the Visual Arts Complex, then take a slow lap through the galleries and compare one work each before heading out.
cards.short_summary: A campus gallery visit with no admission fee.
cards.evidence_claim: CU Art Museum states that there is no fee for admission and that it is free for all visitors.
cards.source_title: Visit | Art Museum | University of Colorado Boulder
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Saturday, 10 a.m.–4 p.m.; check the museum page for football-game Saturday closures.

cards.title: Read or work at Norlin Library
cards.subtitle: Norlin Library, CU Boulder
cards.notes: Bring a book, a class reading, or a shared research question and settle into a public reading session without needing to borrow anything.
cards.short_summary: Use materials on site or spend time in CU Boulder’s main library.
cards.evidence_claim: University Libraries are open to all and provide free onsite access to most materials, including databases.
cards.source_title: University Libraries Circulation Policy | University Libraries | University of Colorado Boulder
cards.access_notes: Onsite use is free; checkout and off-campus electronic access vary by borrower status.

cards.title: Use the Boulder Public Library
cards.subtitle: 1001 Arapahoe Ave, Boulder
cards.notes: Use the public seating or connect to guest Wi-Fi for a low-key work session; save printing or copying for another time if avoiding costs.
cards.short_summary: A public-library hang with free guest wireless internet.
cards.evidence_claim: Boulder Public Library District provides free wireless internet at all library locations, with no password required.
cards.source_title: Computers, Internet & Printing | Boulder Public Library District
cards.access_notes: Guest Wi-Fi is free; printing and copying have listed per-page charges.

cards.title: Walk Chautauqua Park
cards.subtitle: Chautauqua Park, Boulder
cards.notes: Walk the park’s open areas with a friend, stay on designated routes, and check seasonal parking conditions before choosing how to arrive.
cards.short_summary: A self-directed outdoor hang at a named Boulder park.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Boulder fee schedule says no fees are associated with open access to parks, park amenities, pathways and natural areas.
cards.source_title: Parks and Recreation Fee Schedule | City of Boulder
cards.access_notes: Open-access use has no fee; summer weekend and holiday parking near Chautauqua may be paid.

cards.title: Stroll the Boulder Creek Path
cards.subtitle: Boulder Creek Path, Boulder
cards.notes: Choose a short out-and-back segment, pause at a safe public overlook, and keep the group together around cyclists and other path users.
cards.short_summary: A no-fee walk along Boulder’s named creek corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Boulder fee schedule identifies open access to pathways as having no associated fees.
cards.source_title: Parks and Recreation Fee Schedule | City of Boulder
cards.access_notes: This is open-access pathway use; observe posted conditions and shared-path rules.

cards.title: Sit and catch up at Central Park
cards.subtitle: Central Park, Boulder
cards.notes: Bring a conversation, sketchbook, or a simple card game and use the open park area without reserving a facility or special-event space.
cards.short_summary: A downtown park hang that does not require an admission purchase.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Boulder fee schedule says open access to parks and park amenities has no associated fees.
cards.source_title: Parks and Recreation Fee Schedule | City of Boulder
cards.access_notes: Open access is free; reservations and special events can carry separate fees.

cards.title: Have a daylight park meetup
cards.subtitle: North Boulder Park, Boulder
cards.notes: Pick a daylight time, meet at the open park, and keep the plan simple: conversation, a walk around the grounds, or quiet time together.
cards.short_summary: A named city park for a self-directed, no-fee meetup.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Boulder fee schedule says no fees are associated with open access to parks, amenities, pathways and natural areas.
cards.source_title: Parks and Recreation Fee Schedule | City of Boulder
cards.access_notes: Free for open access; do not assume reserved shelters, courts, or programmed activities are free.

cards.title: Take a park walk at Harlow Platts
cards.subtitle: Harlow Platts Park, Boulder
cards.notes: Use the open park for a relaxed walk and conversation, then leave shared areas clear rather than occupying any reservable shelter or court.
cards.short_summary: A straightforward outdoor hang at a named Boulder park.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Boulder fee schedule classifies open access to parks and park amenities as having no associated fees.
cards.source_title: Parks and Recreation Fee Schedule | City of Boulder
cards.access_notes: Open-access use is free; the City lists park-shelter rentals separately.

cards.title: Meet outdoors at Valmont City Park
cards.subtitle: Valmont City Park, Boulder
cards.notes: Use the general open park space for a walk, conversation, or people-watching; skip equipment rentals and reserved facilities to keep it free.
cards.short_summary: A no-purchase outdoor hang in a named city park.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Boulder fee schedule states that open access to parks, amenities, pathways and natural areas has no associated fees.
cards.source_title: Parks and Recreation Fee Schedule | City of Boulder
cards.access_notes: General open access is free; rentals, reservations, and specialized recreation uses may have fees.

cards.title: Visit East Boulder Dog Park with a dog
cards.subtitle: 5660 Sioux Dr, Boulder
cards.notes: If someone in the group has a well-managed dog, meet during daylight, follow leash rules on approach, and stay attentive to the animal’s comfort.
cards.short_summary: A free public dog-park visit for groups with a dog.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Boulder says its dog parks are free and open to the public from dawn to dusk.
cards.access_notes: Free and public from dawn to dusk; bring a dog only if you can follow the city’s posted dog-park rules.
